answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a fixed deposit of copper-backed credits for a cooling period before it can vote or claim rewards. Accounts that coordinate to exceed a spending or voting limit forfeit their deposits, while honest users recover theirs after the period. This does not prove who controls an identity, but it makes a Sybil attack costly: the attacker must fund many deposits and keep that capital unavailable, even if the identities use velvet names or hide behind shale proxies.
